<header><p>Separate Day 4 Session 1 worksheet. Begin with pages 1-2 independently and use the separately supplied four-page report. Later use pages 3-5 for source-based ratings and feedback. No AI exercise is required.</p><button onclick="window.print()">Print worksheet</button></header>

<div class="sheet-page" id="H10-independent-a">

## Page 1 | Independent reading, Q1-Q3

**Name or identifier:** __________________ **Date:** __________________

Read **Sections 1, 2 and 5** of the separately supplied **GreenWaste evaluation report**. Work alone, without AI or discussion. Keep the report open and cite paragraphs such as **R2.1** or **Table T10**.

### Q1 | Outcome and scope

Using the pilot row, name the outcome, units, period and population described. Cite the source.

<div class="writing log-space"></div>

### Q2 | Comparison and fairness

Who is compared in the pilot? Explain why that comparison can be fair, rather than only naming the groups. Cite the source.

<div class="writing log-space"></div>

### Q3 | Estimate, interval and rule

Write the pilot estimate and 95% interval with consistent units and signs. Explain what the interval says about the authority's 1,000 AED rule.

<div class="writing log-space"></div>

**Continue with Q4-Q5 on page 2 before discussing your answers.**

<p class="caption">These responses assess reading from a source, not recall of yesterday's numbers. Positive-saving or negative-cost-difference wording is acceptable when the interval and meaning are consistent.</p>

</div>

<div class="sheet-page" id="H10-independent-b">

## Page 2 | Independent reading, Q4-Q5

**Name or identifier:** __________________

### Q4 | An important concern from the source

Name one important concern, cite the exact report passage and explain why it matters for the decision. Acceptable concerns need not all be the same.

<div class="writing log-space"></div>

### Q5 | Advice that the evidence supports, and an evidence request

Give a recommendation the stated evidence can support. Request one specific document or result and explain how its answer could change your advice.

<div class="writing log-space"></div>

### My opening judgement

**Sign off / With conditions / Request evidence**

My source-based reason:

<div class="writing tall"></div>

<p class="caption">Finish independently before comparing choices. Your recommendation is judged by its evidence and limits, not by selecting a required option. These opening responses will be collected or copied; later revisions are recorded separately.</p>

</div>

<div class="sheet-page">

## Page 3 | Rate an executive-summary claim

Read **R1.1-R1.3** and follow the selected claim to its sources.

**Supported:** the source supports the claim within its limits.  
**Concern:** a specific uncertainty or missing check could change the judgement.  
**Unsupported:** the claim exceeds or contradicts its source.

### A supported passage

Exact paragraph/claim and the checking source:

<div class="writing tall"></div>

Why this claim is supported:

<div class="writing tall"></div>

### An important concern or an unsupported claim

Exact paragraph/claim and the checking source:

<div class="writing tall"></div>

Rating and reason:

<div class="writing tall"></div>

Evidence that could change my judgement:

<div class="writing tall"></div>

### My Wall Sheet 1 note

**Paragraph/claim → rating word → reason.** No name on the wall.

<div class="writing"></div>

<p class="caption">Wall Sheet 1 is the executive-summary A1 grid. It is not worksheet page 1. Rate a named claim; another claim in the same section may deserve a different rating.</p>

</div>

<div class="sheet-page">

Paragraph ID, claim and source-based reason:

**Paragraph/claim → rating word → reason.** No names.

### During the wall discussion

Are we rating the same claim? Which passage explains any difference?

<div class="writing tall"></div>

<p class="caption">Wall Sheet 2 is the A1 grid for Sections 3-7. A Supported disclosure can coexist with an unresolved issue; the rating does not mean every limitation is resolved.</p>
